claims.text: In ARISTOTLE (NCT00412984), apixaban reduced the rate of adjudicated stroke/systemic embolism versus warfarin during the intended treatment period.
In ARISTOTLE, the secondary composite endpoint of stroke/systemic embolism/major bleeding in warfarin/VKA-naive participants also favored apixaban versus warfarin.
In the post-operative atrial fibrillation study (NCT02889562), no strokes were observed in either apixaban or warfarin groups over 30 days.
In the cardioversion study (NCT02100228), apixaban had 0 acute stroke events and 0 systemic embolism events reported in the primary outcome tables.
In the extended-treatment VTE study (NCT00633893), apixaban 2.5 mg showed a lower risk of symptomatic recurrent VTE or all-cause death versus placebo.
In the knee-replacement study (NCT00371683), apixaban 2.5 mg BID had lower event rates than enoxaparin for major/clinically relevant bleeding and for the composite VTE endpoint.

In the bariatric PK study (NCT02406885), apixaban exposure endpoints (Cmax and AUC) were reported for oral solution versus nasogastric tube administration, indicating pharmacokinetic rather than clinical efficacy outcomes.

claims.text: Apixaban Accord is approved in the EU as a medicinal product with SmPC and package leaflet included in the regulatory document set.

The EU SmPC states adult indications for prevention of stroke and systemic embolism in non-valvular atrial fibrillation, treatment of DVT and PE, prevention of recurrent DVT and PE, and prevention of VTE after elective hip or knee replacement surgery (for the 2.5 mg strength).
The EU SmPC includes a paediatric indication for treatment of venous thromboembolism and prevention of recurrent VTE in patients from 28 days to less than 18 years of age.
The SmPC notes that the European Medicines Agency has deferred the obligation to submit results of studies for treatment of venous thromboembolism in one or more subsets of the paediatric population.
The EU regulatory documents show two marketed strengths for Apixaban Accord: 2.5 mg and 5 mg film-coated tablets.

US documents also note prior adult indications for prophylaxis of DVT/PE after hip or knee replacement surgery and treatment of DVT/PE with reduction in recurrence risk after initial therapy.

risks.description: Patients receiving neuraxial anesthesia or spinal puncture while on ELIQUIS are at risk of spinal/epidural hematomas, which may cause long-term or permanent paralysis.
